clue.text: Key is taken by heel and it's not spotted

parts.note: C is a musical key
a ship heels when it leans over to one side

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a heel bears the key and stays free of marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken by' just puts the two pieces together: C first, then LEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without spots or stains is spotless, i.e. free of dirt.

clue.text: A record confirmed by the French

parts.note: confirmed, as in a habit firmly established, means chronic
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Something documented and verified by the French authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link; CHRONIC comes in the sense of a 'confirmed' bachelor or smoker.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicle is a historical account of events in order.

clue.text: Nibbled at in the latter part of the day

indicators.note: 'in' places at inside the word for evening

parts.words: the latter part of the day
parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of evening
taken as written

explanation.surface: Snacked on something in the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: EEN (e'en, poetic for evening) holds AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nibbled has been consumed bit by bit.

clue.text: Tasty morsels of lamb for one to prepare in minutes

indicators.note: 'in' puts one and prepare inside the word for minutes

parts.note: minutes of a meeting are notes
I is the Roman numeral one
to set is to prepare, as in setting a table

explanation.surface: Delicious lamb pieces one can make ready in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' looks like time but is the record of a meeting; 'for' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Small round boneless cuts of meat, typically lamb, are given this French name.

clue.text: Fit for service in the main

definitions.text: Fit for service in the main

parts.words: Fit for service in the main
parts.note: 'the main' is the open ocean, so a vessel fit to serve out there is meant, while the surface suggests chiefly suitable for work

explanation.definitionFit: A ship in good enough condition to sail the open sea is described this way.

clue.text: To make a point reveal blunders — quite a number

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass

indicators.note: 'blunders' suggests reveal goes wrong and its letters end up out of order

explanation.surface: Making a point by exposing a good many mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunders' rearranges REVEAL into EVERAL; 'To make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: More than two but not many, i.e. a fair number.

clue.text: Summarise a game

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Giving a summary of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text while keeping its sense is to condense it.

clue.text: He has to acknowledge Her Majesty's letters

parts.note: to own up is to acknowledge
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A man is obliged to confirm receipt of royal correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He has' defines one who possesses something.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessor is a person who has something as property.

clue.text: A man isn't a spoilt individual down under

indicators.note: 'spoilt' means the letters of A man isn't a are spoiled and reshuffled

explanation.surface: A man who is not a pampered person in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' is Australia; the answer is someone from the island state south of the mainland.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Australian island state, so a person from down under.

clue.text: It is indeed the way to raise dough

definitions.text: It is indeed the way to raise dough

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed
St is street, a way

explanation.surface: This really is how you make bread rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it and gives YEA + ST; 'It is' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungus added to bread mixture makes it rise by fermentation.

clue.text: Working dog — all-out trier at all times

indicators.note: 'all-out' suggests the letters of trier are thrown out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: ever means always, at all times

explanation.surface: A tireless working dog that never stops trying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all-out' reads as describing the trier's effort, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gundog breed trained to fetch shot game is a classic working dog.

clue.text: Make a home with a woman

parts.note: birds nest when they build a home

explanation.surface: Settling down to set up house with a female partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it stands for a woman in crossword convention.

clue.text: Nobody has caught cold for the present

indicators.note: 'has caught' means the word for nobody holds the cold letter inside it

parts.note: none means no one, nobody
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: No one has picked up a chill at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the nonce' is the idiom for 'for the present', so 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the current occasion, as in the idiom 'for the nonce' = for now.

clue.text: The flier taking bread maybe — and everything else around

indicators.note: 'around' says the word for everything else surrounds the scrambled bread

parts.note: rest means the remainder, everything else

indicators.note: 'maybe' signals that bread may be another arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A garden bird pecking at bread, among all the other creatures about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges 'bread'; 'taking' is a link word. The bird is the robin.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin, a common garden bird with a red chest, is known by this name.

clue.text: Assets invested in London?

definitions.meaning: money and assets put into a business
London is the chief city of the UK, so an example of a nation's seat of government

explanation.surface: Money put into property in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both money invested in an enterprise and a country's chief city, London being one.

clue.text: Contracting to put note in purse? Just the opposite!

annotationWithheld.why: Contracting to put note in purse? Just the opposite! (9) for PUCKERING: no parse found that builds the letters from 'note' and 'purse' with the reversal 'Just the opposite!'
annotationWithheld.clue: Contracting to put note in purse? Just the opposite!

clue.text: The listener may be pierced by this

definitions.text: The listener may be pierced by this

parts.words: The listener may be pierced by this
parts.note: 'the listener' is the ear itself, and jewellery worn on it goes through a pierced lobe

explanation.definitionFit: A piece of jewellery worn through a hole in the ear lobe.

clue.text: Restriction the country's to bring back

parts.note: a rein is a check or restraint
a state is a country

explanation.surface: A nation's curbs are to be restored.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone or something to a former position.

clue.text: Bed-makers

parts.note: not people who tidy sheets but those who make flower beds in the garden

explanation.definitionFit: People who dig and plant flower beds in a garden.

clue.text: Cut tax by five hundred

parts.note: excise is a tax on goods
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A government reducing a tax by 500.
explanation.definitionFit: To excise something is to cut it out surgically or remove it.

clue.text: Half made a stand, and that most highly valued

indicators.note: 'Half' takes the second half of the word made

parts.note: a rest is a stand or support

explanation.surface: Someone half built a stall, the thing they cherished most.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of MADE gives DE; then A and REST; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Most cherished or beloved, superlative of a word meaning loved.

clue.text: Turner, a lawbreaker when without money

indicators.note: 'without' in its old sense of outside, so the lawbreaker goes around the money

parts.note: a sinner breaks moral or divine law
P is penny, a small sum of money

explanation.surface: A turner who turns to crime when he is broke.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinner in cricket is a bowler who turns the ball, hence 'Turner'; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin bowler in cricket makes the ball turn off the pitch.

clue.text: Retired person supporting public transport

definitions.meaning: one who has retired for the night, i.e. gone to bed and is asleep
a beam under railway track, holding up the rails

explanation.surface: A pensioner who backs buses and trains.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both someone asleep and a railway tie that supports the rails.

clue.text: Declare the head must hold back alcoholic drink

indicators.note: 'must hold' means the word for the head contains the other piece

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head

indicators.note: 'back' says the drink's name is written in the opposite direction

parts.note: cider is fermented apple drink

explanation.surface: An order that the boss must keep off the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The head' looks like a boss but is simply the top of the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate something is to assert or affirm it as true.

clue.text: A model's brain-teaser

definitions.meaning: one who poses for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A fashion model's puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both someone posing and a puzzling problem.

clue.text: Thought the novice exemplary

parts.note: an idea is a thought
L is a learner, a novice

explanation.surface: Thinking the beginner is a perfect example.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect, serving as a model to follow.

clue.text: Post the collateral

definitions.meaning: a pointed wooden pole driven into the ground
something put up as a pledge or security, as in a bet

explanation.surface: Posting the security for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a pointed upright pole and an amount pledged or wagered.

clue.text: A strike to cause embarrassment

parts.note: to bash is to strike hard

explanation.surface: A blow that leaves someone red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone feel ashamed or disconcerted.

clue.text: A quarter rent some land

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: Leasing a section of an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: A SHIRE is an English county, a division of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A county is a region of territory, so a tract of land.

clue.text: Set off, and please walk

indicators.note: 'Set off' suggests the letters are set off in a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: An invitation to start out on a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' rearranges AND and PLEASE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade along a seafront is a public place to stroll.

clue.text: The governor turning over a gun to rebel leader

indicators.note: 'turning over' says a and the gun's name are read in reverse

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol
taken as written

indicators.note: 'leader' means the opening letter of the word rebel

explanation.surface: An official who turns a weapon over to the head of the rebels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning over' turns A LUGER into REGULA; then TO and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor in engineering is a device controlling speed or flow, i.e. a control mechanism.

clue.text: Creating a bit of a racket, hospital staff show characteristic spirit

indicators.note: 'a bit of' says only part of the words racket, hospital is needed, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: Noisy hospital staff showing their true colours.
explanation.definitionFit: The distinctive character or guiding beliefs of a group or culture.
